message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes of all time. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School before being selected first overall in the 2003 NBA Draft by the Cleveland Cavaliers.

James has played for the Cleveland Cavaliers (2003–2010, 2014–2018), Miami Heat (2010–2014), and Los Angeles Lakers (2018–present). He has won four NBA championships—two with Miami (2012, 2013), one with Cleveland (2016), and one with Los Angeles (2020)—and earned four NBA Finals MVP awards. In addition to his championship success, he has been named NBA Most Valuable Player (MVP) four times (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013) and has been selected to the All‑NBA First Team 13 times.

Beyond the court, LeBron is known for his philanthropy, notably the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the “I Promise” school in Akron to support at-risk youth. He has also pursued acting, producing, and business ventures, including a partnership with Nike and ownership stakes in media companies such as SpringHill Entertainment.
